did_you_know.text: Did you know? The vision opens with a gate facing east—the direction from which the glory of the God of Israel would come to the temple.
Did you know? The voice of the LORD’s glory is described as the sound of many waters, and the whole land shines with his glory—a description emphasizing the power and extent of the revelation.
Did you know? Ezekiel identifies the sight with earlier visions: the vision of the LORD’s glory that he saw when the city was destroyed, and the visions he saw by the Kebar River.
Did you know? The glory of the LORD enters the temple through the east gate, the same direction from which it came at the beginning of the vision.

Did you know? The LORD declares that the temple will be the place of his throne and the place for the soles of his feet, and that he will dwell among the Israelites forever. However, Israel must remove their impurity and detestable practices.
Did you know? Ezekiel is commanded to present the design of the temple to the people of Israel so that they may be ashamed of their sins and pay attention to its structure and dimensions.
Did you know? The law of the temple summarizes its description by declaring that the entire area surrounding it on the mountaintop is most holy.
Did you know? The description of the altar uses measurements in cubits and handbreadths and details its stepped sections, from the foundation to the upper surface.
Did you know? The altar is described as square, and at the end of the description of its dimensions, it is noted that the steps—that is, the ramp or stairs—face east.
Did you know? The dedication of the altar lasts seven days. From the eighth day onward, the sacrificial service begins, and the LORD promises to accept the Israelites.
